h1: The 7 Best Folding Wheelchair Ramps to Carry, Store and Trust, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Folding Wheelchair Ramps: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 folding portable wheelchair ramps from 3 to 8 feet, compared on slope, weight, capacity, baffles and folded size for carrying.
summary: The FACHNUO 8FT ramp with support legs is the best folding ramp for taller entries, with side baffles and reflective strips. The TaiH Leo 8FT is the close alternative, the HYUNAN METHOD 4FT is the best mid-length ramp, and the HYUNAN METHOD 3FT is the lightest full-width ramp for one or two low steps.
intro: A folding ramp is judged twice: once when you use it, and again when you lift it. A ramp that performs well on a porch but weighs too much to carry to the car will end up left at home, which defeats the point of portability. That is why folded size and weight deserve as much attention as the rated capacity, and why a folding ramp should always be tested at the entrance it will serve before you rely on it.

We reviewed seven aluminum folding ramps from 3 to 8 feet long, ranked on slope suitability, side protection, weight, folded size and capacity. We keep to the commonly cited 1:12 guideline, one inch of rise for every foot of ramp, and treat the high end of each listed rise range as something that calls for a helper. Ask a clinician or the maker if you are unsure about a particular chair or rise.

products.name: FACHNUO 8FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp With Support Legs
products.verdict: An 8 foot folding ramp with support legs, side baffles and reflective strips.
products.description:
The FACHNUO 8FT ramp folds to a 4 foot package and has support legs, side baffles and reflective strips. The maker lists it for rises of 8 to 24 inches, and it costs $200 to $500.

Braced length and edge protection are what push it to the top. An 8 foot ramp is long enough to handle an 8 inch step on the 1:12 guideline, the legs stop the middle from bowing under weight, and the baffles keep wheels from drifting off the edge. Reflective strips are a small but welcome safety touch at night. It is bulkier than the shorter models when folded.

Buy it for a porch or a vehicle entry that rises about 8 inches. Use a helper on anything much taller.
pros: Folds to a four foot package
products.idealFor: Porches and vehicle entries around 8 inches high.
products.skipIf: You need something small for travel.

products.name: TaiH Leo 8FT Wheelchair Ramp With Support Legs
products.verdict: A braced 8 foot folding ramp for porches and van entries with an 8 to 16 inch rise.
products.description:
The TaiH Leo is an 8 foot ramp that folds in half to a roughly 4 foot by 14 inch package, with adjustable support legs and a listed rise range of 8 to 24 inches. It costs $200 to $500.

It ranks a hair behind the FACHNUO because the listing does not mention side baffles or reflective strips, though the adjustable legs are a plus on uneven ground. Both give you the same length and the same bracing idea. If your ground is not level, the TaiH's adjustable legs may win it for you.

Buy it for a porch or van entry that needs a supported span. Confirm edge protection with the seller.
pros: Folds to a compact four foot package
Same price tier as the FACHNUO
products.idealFor: Porches and van entries on uneven ground.
products.skipIf: You want side baffles on the listing.

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 4FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: A documented 4 foot folding ramp with an 800 pound rating, at 18.43 pounds.
products.description:
The HYUNAN METHOD 4FT ramp weighs 18.43 pounds, carries 800 pounds and folds in half for transport. The listing gives a rise range of 4 to 12 inches, and it costs $100 to $200.

It places third because it is the most thoroughly documented mid-size folding ramp, with weight, capacity and folded dimensions all printed. A four-foot ramp suits a four-inch step on the 1:12 guideline, which covers many entry thresholds and curbs. At 18.43 pounds, one person can carry it, which is not true of the 8 foot models.

Buy it for low steps up to about 4 inches. Treat the 12 inch top of the listed range as needing help.
products.idealFor: Low steps and curbs, with a carry-friendly weight.
products.skipIf: Your step is much taller than 4 inches.

products.name: VNN Portable Wheelchair Ramp 6FT Seamless
products.verdict: A 6 foot ramp with a seamless center hinge that tools are not needed to fold.
products.description:
The VNN 6FT ramp has a seamless center hinge, a double non-skid surface and folds without tools. The listing gives a rise range of 6 to 18 inches, and it costs $200 to $500.

A seam in the middle of a ramp is a small bump, but small casters and walker wheels feel it, and the seamless hinge is built to remove that jolt. Six feet suits a six inch step on the 1:12 guideline, so it fits many porch steps. It ranks fourth because it lacks support legs, which long folding ramps usually need for stiffness.

Buy it for a six inch porch step where ride quality matters. Skip it for anything much taller.
products.idealFor: Six inch porch steps with small wheels.
products.skipIf: Your rise is above about 8 inches.

products.award: Best Edge Protection on a Short Ramp
products.name: FACHNUO 3FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: A 3 foot ramp with side baffles, reflective strips and a pleated deck for grip.
products.description:
The FACHNUO 3FT ramp has baffles at the sides, reflective strips and a pleated deck, with a listed fit for rises of 3 to 9 inches. It costs $100 to $200 and suits walker and chair users.

Edge protection is rare on a ramp this short, and it matters because small ramps are used by people who are least able to correct a wheel drifting sideways. The pleated surface adds traction. At three feet it suits a three-inch step on the 1:12 guideline, so the listed 9 inch top is not realistic without help.

Buy it for a single low step. Choose the longer FACHNUO for anything taller.
pros: Side baffles on a short ramp
products.idealFor: A single low step with walker or chair users.
products.skipIf: Your step is taller than about 4 inches.

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 3FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.verdict: A 14.02 pound, 800 pound capacity ramp for one or two low steps.
products.description:
The HYUNAN METHOD 3FT ramp weighs 14.02 pounds, carries 800 pounds and folds to a package about a foot and a quarter wide. It costs $50 to $100, which is the lowest tier in the ranking.

It lands sixth because three feet limits the rise it can serve, and the listing does not mention baffles or reflective strips that the FACHNUO 3FT adds. In its favor, the weight is low, the capacity is generous and the price is the cheapest here, so it is a sensible stash for a car trunk.

Buy it for one or two low steps and a light carry. Pair it with an assistant for any larger step.
pros: Easy to store in a trunk
products.idealFor: A light trunk ramp for one or two low steps.
products.skipIf: You need edge protection or more length.

products.name: KOLOTOOL Portable Wheelchair Ramps 3FT
products.verdict: A non-skid aluminum 3 foot ramp that folds in half for visits to homes with one step.
products.description:
The KOLOTOOL 3FT ramp is made of non-skid aluminum, folds in half and holds 800 pounds. The listed rise range is 3 to 9 inches, and it costs $100 to $200.

It finishes last because it costs about as much as the FACHNUO 3FT and more than the HYUNAN 3FT, without side baffles or a stated weight. As a stand-by ramp for visits to a relative's home with one low step, it is a reasonable choice that fits in a closet.

Buy it for occasional visits where one low step is the only barrier. Choose a baffled or lighter model for regular use.
products.idealFor: Occasional visits to homes with a single low step.
products.skipIf: You want edge protection or a lighter ramp.

methodology.title: Slope suitability
methodology.description: We matched each ramp's length to the rise it can serve on the 1:12 guideline, and treated the upper end of every listed rise range as needing a helper.

methodology.title: Edge and traction safety
methodology.description: Side baffles, reflective strips, non-skid and pleated surfaces were credited for keeping wheels on the ramp.

methodology.title: Weight and carry
methodology.description: We compared stated ramp weights, from 14 pounds up, since a ramp you cannot lift will not be used.

methodology.title: Capacity and support
methodology.description: Weight ratings such as 800 pounds and support legs on 8 foot models were weighed for strength under load.

methodology.title: Folded size and price
methodology.description: Folded dimensions and price tiers from $50 to $500 were compared, within the limit of what each listing prints.

whatMatters.detail: The 1:12 guideline asks for one foot of ramp per inch of rise. A four-inch step wants four feet, and an eight-inch porch wants eight. Measure the rise, then choose a length that respects the ratio rather than the maker's widest range.

Baffles are raised edges that stop a wheel from rolling off the side, which is a real risk on narrow ramps. They matter most for people using walkers or manual chairs. Look for baffles or guardrails on the listing.
A non-skid, pleated or double-textured deck grips wheels and shoes in rain. Smooth aluminum becomes slippery when wet. Check that the deck has a stated traction treatment.
Lighter ramps are easier to carry, but long ramps stay bulky even when folded. Compare the folded length with your car trunk. Look at the carry handle too.
Ramps of 6 feet or more can flex in the middle, and legs hold the span steady. Adjustable legs help on uneven ground. Test the ramp with a helper before relying on it.

howToChoose.intro: Length is the main choice, because it decides how steep the slope will be at a given rise.

cards.label: Light carry
cards.text: Ramps of 3 to 4 feet that one person can lift. The HYUNAN 3FT and 4FT, FACHNUO 3FT and KOLOTOOL 3FT fit this style.

cards.label: Braced span
cards.text: Longer ramps with support legs for porches and vans. The FACHNUO 8FT and TaiH Leo 8FT are built for it.

howToChoose.note: Choose a light carry ramp for curbs and single steps, and a braced span for anything taller than about 6 inches.

howToChoose.subheading: For Travel and Car Trunks Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A weight under about 20 pounds, a fold-in-half design and a carry handle. Check the folded length against your trunk.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The HYUNAN METHOD 3FT at 14.02 pounds is the lightest, and the 4FT is the best compromise of length and weight.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The rise is above 6 inches or the ramp is used daily. The FACHNUO and TaiH 8 foot models at $200 to $500 give a safer slope.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need to cross a single low step. The HYUNAN METHOD 3FT at $50 to $100 is enough.

faq.q: How do I choose a ramp length?
faq.a: Measure the vertical rise and allow one foot of ramp per inch. A longer ramp is always gentler. Ask a clinician for advice if the user has limited strength.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with folding ramps?
faq.a: Trusting the maker's rise range. A short ramp on a tall step is steep and unsafe without help. Use the length that matches the rise.

faq.q: Is a portable ramp worth it over a threshold ramp?
faq.a: For steps and curbs, yes, because threshold ramps are too short. A portable folding ramp can serve several locations. For a single doorway sill, a threshold ramp is simpler.

faq.q: How do I set up a folding ramp?
faq.a: Unfold on a flat surface, extend any legs and rest the top edge on the step with no gap. Make sure it cannot slide. Test with an assistant before use.
Fold it and store it in a dry spot, in a closet, trunk or garage. Keep it flat to avoid warping. Wipe the surface clean first.

faq.q: Can I leave a ramp outdoors?
faq.a: Aluminum resists rust, but leaving a ramp outside exposes it to ice and debris. Bring it in when not in use. Clear snow and ice before every use.

finalTake: The FACHNUO 8FT with support legs and baffles is the best folding ramp for taller entries, and the TaiH Leo 8FT is the alternative if your ground is uneven. The HYUNAN METHOD 4FT is the pick for low steps and easy carrying, with the FACHNUO 3FT as a short ramp with edge protection. Always choose length by rise, and bring a helper for steeper slopes.
